auditor_value: (a) |dv/dt| is the magnitude of the acceleration vector, which includes both the change of speed and the change of direction; d|v|/dt is the rate of change of speed alone. (b) They are equal when the acceleration is along the velocity, that is straight-line motion in which the speed is increasing; in uniform circular motion d|v|/dt = 0 while |dv/dt| = v²/R.

findings.quote: In straight-line motion the direction of velocity never changes, so the entire acceleration goes into changing the speed, and the two quantities are equal.
findings.note: Straight-line motion alone is not sufficient. If the object moves in a straight line while slowing down, d|v|/dt is negative while |dv/dt| is positive: for v = (5 − 2t) along x, |dv/dt| = 2 m/s² but d|v|/dt = −2 m/s² at t = 1 s. Equality needs the acceleration to point along the velocity, that is the speed increasing. The same claim is repeated in steps[2].equation and in final_answer.value.
findings.fix: When the acceleration is along the velocity, so that the object moves in a straight line with its speed increasing, the whole acceleration changes the speed and the two quantities are equal; if it moves in a straight line while slowing down, d|v|/dt is negative and equals −|dv/dt|.

notes: Parts (a), the circular-motion example and the mistake entry are correct; the only defect is the unqualified claim of equality for all straight-line motion.
